criteria.note: A versioned decision-record format (schema warp.decision/v1) is defined in .warp/decision.py. validate_record requires id, title, status, problem_class, owner (non-empty strings), an integer version >= 1, a non-empty options list (each option an id, a summary, and its dead_end condition), and a non-empty assumptions list (each an id, a statement, a signal, and a breach); a record with no assumptions is refused (I reproduced this over the real example: 'no assumptions: a decision record carries the assumptions that become living tripwires'). Records are homed per-repo under .warp/decisions/*.yaml, a subdirectory the single-level .warp/*.yaml engine glob does not sweep; I confirmed no .warp/decisions/ directory ships anywhere (root, plugin/templates, or any pack). The illustrative example ships at .warp/examples/decision-example.yaml in the un-decided draft state with no attributed decider; I ran python3 .warp/validate.py decisions .warp/examples/decision-example.yaml -> rc 0, and the selftest asserts the example is present, status: draft, with no decided_by (I verified both directly). check_decision is exercised in the gate via the run_all examples block (confirmed live: 'decision-example.yaml' present in run_all source).

The validator (.warp/decision.py, invoked by validate.py check_decision/check_decisions and gate-run via validate.py all) fails closed BY NAME on each claimed class, and I proved it by mutating the REAL shipped example on disk and observing python3 .warp/validate.py decisions go rc 1 with the correct message, then reverting byte-identical. Verified live over the real example: wrong schema id ('schema must be warp.decision/v1'), non-integer version ('version must be an integer >= 1'; also caught version: true and version: 0), out-of-vocab status ('bad status'), out-of-vocab reversal_cost ('reversal_cost must be one of'), out-of-vocab risk ('risk must be one of'), an option lacking its dead_end ('option db_poll: a dead_end condition is required'; also caught a non-string list-valued dead_end), duplicate option id ('duplicate option id'), duplicate assumption id ('duplicate assumption id'), and a tab-indented malformed file (surfaced as 'decision record outside the record subset: tab indentation ... space-indented only', DecisionRecordError -> fail closed). decision.py imports only 'from pathlib import Path' and receives parse_yamlish and fail from validate.py (confirmed by source read), so there is no second YAML parser and no import cycle. The well-formed example validates clean, so the check cannot pass vacuously.

Governance is enforced: only a human decides, on the record (O4, NG2). In validate_record, status == 'decided' requires a decision block with decided_by, decided_at, and a chosen option that resolves to a declared option, or it fails closed ('only a human decides, on the record' / 'never machine-decided' / 'referenced but absent'); a draft needs no decider; and a non-decided record that carries a decision block with a decider or a chosen option is refused ('never by smuggling a decision under a draft'). D5 is mechanized: reversal_cost 'irreversible' at a risk tier other than 'critical' fails closed ('reversal_cost irreversible must map to risk critical (D5)'). I proved every direction over the REAL example: flip to decided with no block -> RED; decided with a block but no decider -> RED; chosen names a non-existent option -> RED ('decision.chosen ghost_option is not a declared option'); draft smuggling a decider -> RED; irreversible left at risk high -> RED; and the positives (a draft validates; the real example flipped to a fully decided, resolving record validates; irreversible+critical validates) all rc 0. No machine-decided state is representable. Matches the plan's W5 intent and the D5 resolution (irreversible -> critical) exactly; the two-verdict scrutiny itself is correctly deferred to WARP-1106. See NOTE 1 on the superseded lifecycle and NOTE 2 on a lone decided_at, both non-blocking.

findings.text: HONESTY / OVER-ATTESTATION JUDGMENT (step 4): CORRECT boundary, no over-attestation. The builder shipped the format, the validator, and a clearly-marked DRAFT example (id DEC-0000, owner 'the-human-accountable-for-this-choice', status: draft, NO decided_by) and deliberately did NOT create a 'decided' foundational record. This is exactly the honest call and directly applies the WARP-1101 review lesson: recording a human as having decided a foundational choice they did not actually make (through the WARP-1106 adversarial review, which does not exist yet) would be a false attestation, so no such record was manufactured. I confirmed no human is recorded as deciding anything anywhere (no .warp/decisions/ directory ships; the example has no decided_by), and that the validator makes machine-decided state structurally unrepresentable (a decided record requires a recorded human decider or it fails closed; a draft may not smuggle one). The capabilities entry (foundational_decision_record, status: mechanical, home .warp/decision.py) is accurate: the module IS a mechanical structural validator, it ships in the engine, and the entry explicitly names WARP-1106 (adversarial review) and WARP-1107 (in-session tripwire monitoring) as the later consumers rather than claiming them built. No rule is marked mechanizable that nothing enforces: the validator refuses today, and I reproduced its teeth. This is the honest W5 boundary, not a gap.

NOTE 1 (non-blocking, under-specified corner): a 'superseded' record that RETAINS its historical decision block is REJECTED. Because the smuggle guard is an elif over any non-'decided' status, a record with status: superseded + superseded_by that also carries its original decision block (decided_by/chosen) fails closed with 'status superseded carries a decision block with a decider or a chosen option'. That forces a superseded record to drop the audit trail of who originally decided, keeping only the forward superseded_by pointer. This is NOT blocking: (1) the superseded/re-decision lifecycle is explicitly a WARP-1107 concern (the module comment calls the successor 'W7's re-decision draft') and no W5 AC or selftest specifies how a superseded record carries its prior decision; (2) it fails CLOSED (over-strict), never open, so it can only reject a legitimate record, never admit a bad one; (3) nothing produces superseded records yet (W7 is unbuilt), so it is inert today. Recommendation for the W7 builder: decide explicitly whether a superseded record retains its historical decision block, and if so, scope the smuggle guard to the 'draft' status rather than to all non-'decided' statuses.

NOTE 2 (non-blocking hardening): a draft carrying a decision block with ONLY decided_at (no decided_by and no chosen) validates clean. The smuggle guard checks any(_is_str(decision.get(f)) for f in ('decided_by', 'chosen')), so a lone timestamp is not caught. This faithfully matches the AC3 wording ('may not smuggle a decision block carrying a decider or a chosen option') and is harmless: a lone decided_at attributes no decision to any human and names no chosen option, so no machine-decided state and no false attestation is representable. Optional hardening: reject any decision block whatsoever on a non-decided record, so a stray timestamp cannot linger on a draft.

ENVIRONMENTAL PARITY (non-blocking, general to WARP commits): the 'generated' gate check is green because specs/index.md was regenerated at this commit; a rerun on a later day would flip it RED until the index is restamped, the same date-stamp behavior recorded in prior WARP-100x/1101 reviews.
